title: Protocol for using artificial lipid droplets to study the binding affinity of lipid droplet-associated proteins
protocol: Dry phospholipids on the wall of microcentrifuge tube using a stream of N2.
Add neutral lipids and Buffer B to the tube containing dried phospholipids.
Vortex lipid mixture to prepare the lipid emulsion.
Centrifuge at 1,000×g to remove the top fraction.
Centrifuge at 20,000×g to remove the bottom pellet.
The remaining emulsion contains adiposomes.
Prepare phospholipid stock at the concentration described in Table 1.
Transfer 80 μL of phospholipid stock to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Dry the lipids as a thin layer on the wall of the tube using a gentle N2 stream for 2 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Hydrate the dried lipids in 100 μL Buffer B for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Transfer neutral lipids to the buffer at a phospholipid:neutral lipid molar ratio of 1:2, roughly 5 μL triolein per 100 μL aqueous system.
Set the vortex rotation rate to 3,000–4,000 rpm.
Vortex the lipid-buffer mixture for 24 cycles (10 s on and 10 s off).
Centrifuge the emulsion at 1,000×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Collect the infranatant containing small, dispersed lipid particles using a gel-loading pipette tip.
Transfer the collected infranatant to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the new tube containing dispersed lipid particles at 20,000×g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Use a gel-loading pipette tip to collect precipitates at the bottom of the tube carefully.
Leave the dispersed emulsion in the tube.
Add Buffer B to the original tube to achieve a volume of 100 μL.
Vortex the mixture for 10 cycles of 10 seconds on and 10 seconds off.
Centrifuge the mixture again at 1,000×g.
Centrifuge the mixture again at 20,000×g to isolate adiposome product.
Pool adiposomes from two emulsification/purification cycles.
Dilute the original adiposomes 50-fold in Buffer B and stain them using LipidTOX Red or LipidTOX Green for 30 min at 20°C–25°C in the dark, at a volumetric ratio of 1:1,000 (v/v).
Use a laser scanning confocal microscope or other available fluorescence microscope to observe the shape of adiposomes.
Set excitation and emission conditions appropriate for the dye used.
Conduct an additional round of 1,000×g centrifugation if contamination is observed.
Conduct an additional round of 20,000×g centrifugation if contamination is observed.
Purify the product again to reduce contaminations until most are removed.
Use transmission electron microscopy to observe the adiposome ultrastructure after ultrathin sectioning.
Fix 50 μL of adiposomes with an equal volume of 2% glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M sodium phosphate buffer for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Subsequently fix the adiposomes further with 100 μL of 2% osmium tetroxide for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Collect fixed adiposomes by centrifugation at 1,000×g for 5 minutes.
Dehydrate the adiposomes using an ascending concentration gradient of ethanol: 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, and 95%.
Dehydrate the adiposomes thrice with 100% ethanol for 10 minutes in each series (1 mL).
Infiltrate the specimen with Embed 812.
Polymerize the infiltrated specimen.
Prepare 70 nm sections using a Leica EM UC6 Ultramicrotome or similar device.
Stain the sections with uranyl acetate and lead citrate.
Capture images of the specimen with a Tecnai Spirit Electron Microscope or similar.
After ultrathin sectioning, observe the morphology of adiposomes under TEM.
Load 8 μL of isolated adiposomes onto glow-discharged, carbon film coated grids for 1 minute.
Remove excess sample by blotting with filter paper.
Fix samples with 10 μL of 1% osmium tetroxide for 10 minutes.
Wash samples by placing the grid sample-side down on three drops of deionized water sequentially.
Stain samples with 10 μL of 0.1% tannic acid for 5 minutes.
Wash samples similarly after each staining step.
Stain samples with 10 μL of 2% uranyl acetate for 5 minutes.
Capture images using a CM120-FEG (FEI) microscope operating at 100 kV.
Extract total adiposome lipids twice using a mixture of chloroform:methanol:Buffer B (1:1:1, v/v/v).
Mix 100 μL adiposome suspension with 200 μL Buffer B, 300 μL methanol, and then 300 μL chloroform.
Vortex the mixture three times.
Incubate at 25°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge the mixture at 20,000×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer the underneath organic phase to a clean vial.
Repeat extraction by adding 300 μL chloroform into the original tube and vortexing three times.
Incubate again at 25°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge again at 20,000×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Combine the two organic phases in a clean vial.
Dry the combined organic phase using a gentle stream of N2.
Dissolve the dry lipids in 100 μL chloroform.
Apply 10-20 μL sample to a silica gel plate (30–200 μm thickness and 60 Å pore size).
Develop the neutral lipid plate with hexane:diethyl ether:acetic acid = 80:20:1 (v/v/v) solution.
Dry the silica gel plate in a fume hood for 10 min.
Mix chloroform, methanol, acetic acid, and water in a volume ratio of 75:13:9:3 (v/v/v/v) for developing polar lipids.
Develop the silica gel plate in the mixture for approximately 20 min.
Dry the silica gel plate in a fume hood for 10 min.
Visualize separated lipids using either saturated iodine vapor staining or acid staining.
Put the developed plate in a sealed box filled with saturated iodine vapor for at least 15 min and observe or scan the plate immediately.
Spray the plate with a mixture of 8% phosphoric acid (m/m), 10% CuSO4 (m/m) in water to stain lipids as black spots.
Heat the stained plate in an oven at 110°C for 15 min.
Dilute roughly 10–20 μL adiposome sample into 1 mL Buffer B.
Set the measuring temperature as 25°C and perform 70 cycles for each DLS test.
Apply the physical parameters of water at 25°C, which indicates a refractive index of 1.33, viscosity of 0.89 cP, and dielectric constant of 78.50 to the system.
Transform the plasmid into Transetta (DE3) competent cells.
Inoculate each selected clone in 11 mL of LB medium containing 50 μg/mL kanamycin.
Culture clones at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm until OD600 value reaches 0.6.
Transfer 1 mL bacterial cells to 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes for IPTG induction.
Add 0.4 mM IPTG to induce protein expression at 16°C for 24 hours.
Culture another 1 mL of each clone under the same condition without IPTG.
Store remaining 9 mL bacterial cells temporarily at 4°C.
Centrifuge cultured bacterial cells at 20,000×g for 5 minutes and discard supernatant.
Resuspend bacterial cells with 500 μL Tris-NaCl buffer and centrifuge again to remove supernatant.
Add 200 μL of 2 × Sample buffer into the bacteria cells.
Sonicate the mixture on ice for 1 minute (6 seconds on, 6 seconds off) at 210 W.
Boil samples at 95°C for 5 minutes followed by short centrifugation, gentle vortex and another short centrifugation.
Prepare 10-well polyacrylamide gels.
Load samples of each clone, including uninduced and IPTG-induced samples.
Run electrophoresis.
Detect protein expression by Coomassie Brilliant Blue Staining.
Compare the bands of induced sample with those of uninduced sample.
Select clones with strong induction.
Preserve positive clones in 30% glycerol at −80°C.
Inoculate 2 × YT medium containing 50 μg/mL antibiotic kanamycin with protein-expressing bacteria.
Shake the inoculated medium at 37°C, 200 rpm for 4 hours until the OD600 reaches roughly 0.6.
Add 0.4 mM IPTG to induce recombinant protein production.
Incubate at 16°C, 200 rpm for 24 hours.
Collect bacterial cells by centrifuging at 3,000 × g, 16°C for 20 minutes and remove the medium.
Resuspend cells from 800 mL of medium in 30 mL pre-cooled Tris-NaCl buffer.
Centrifuge the suspension at 3,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Repeat resuspension and centrifugation to thoroughly remove residual medium.
Resuspend bacterial cells in pre-cooled Tris-NaCl buffer with 0.5 mM PMSF protease inhibitor.
Break cells using a high pressure cell crusher set at 1,500 Pa and 4°C for three passes.
Collect 20 μL of bacterial lysate as whole cell lysate (WCL) sample for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Centrifuge the cell lysate at 29,761×g (average RCF), 4°C for 50 min using Type 45 Ti tubes.
Collect 20 μL of supernatant sample and pellet for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Pause point: Store the supernatant of cell lysate temporarily at −80°C after mixing with 0.5 mM PMSF protease inhibitor for up to 12 hours.
Recover the supernatant and purify proteins using Ni SepharoseTM 6 Fast Flow, following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Apply the supernatant to the resins three times at a low flow rate with several pauses to ensure thorough binding.
Collect 20 μL liquid as flow through sample (FT).
Wash off nonspecifically bound proteins with 2 column volumes of washing buffer.
Refill the column immediately when the buffer flows to the top interface of the resins.
Add 4 mL elution buffer and label the effluent as 500-elution-1.
Collect 50 μL of the effluent for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Continue applying elution buffer.
Reserve 4–5 mL effluent as 500-elution-2 when the elution buffer reaches half of the column volume.
Collect 50 μL of 500-elution-2 for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Rinse the centrifugal filter devices with 4 mL distilled water followed by another spin of 4 mL Tris-NaCl buffer.
Add 4 mL 500-elution-2 into ultra-centrifugal filter units.
Concentrate 500-elution-2 by centrifuging at 2,500×g for 10 min.
Reconstitute concentrated 500-elution-2 to the original volume with Tris-NaCl buffer.
Repeat the concentration and reconstitution steps.
Transfer 500-elution-2 samples to PCR tubes (100 μL per tube).
Flash-freeze the samples in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C.
Add 2 × sample buffer into each sample (final concentration: 1 ×).
Boil the samples at 95°C for 5 min.
Centrifuge the boiled samples briefly, vortex gently several times, and centrifuge briefly again to precipitate insoluble matters.
Load samples into two 10-well polyacrylamide gels in the order of WCL, S, P, FT, 40-elution, 500-elution-1, 500-elution-2.
Run electrophoresis.
Stain one gel with Coomassie Brilliant Blue and use another for Western blot to identify PLIN2.
Use ultra-centrifugal filter units with an appropriate molecular weight cut-off (MWCO) to concentrate the protein solution.
Centrifuge the protein solution at 2,500×g at 4°C for 10 min.
Replace the elution buffer with Tris-NaCl buffer if necessary.
Repeat the centrifugation procedure if further concentration is needed and precipitates are observed.
Choose an ultra-centrifugal filter unit with a MWCO no more than one third of the molecular weight of the target recombinant protein.
Observe the solution carefully after each centrifugation to ensure clarity and absence of precipitates.
Dilute the stock recombinant protein solution to 1–5 mg/mL.
Transfer 0.1–10 μL of protein solution into 30–200 μL of diluted adiposome suspension (OD600 = 20) in a microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate the suspension at 37°C in a water bath for 5 min.
Centrifuge the suspension at 20,000×g, 4°C for 5 min.
Remove the infranatant using gel-loading pipette tip.
Add buffer to restore the initial volume and gently shake the tube to resuspend the artificial LDs.
Repeat step 33 twice to further remove excess proteins.
Store the artificial LDs at 2°C–8°C until needed.
Use a laser scanning confocal microscope or other available fluorescence microscopes to observe the shape of artificial LDs.
Observe that the artificial LD should be a round shape with a peripheral circle of proteins.
Store adiposomes temporarily at 2°C–8°C.
Determine the number density of adiposomes using an asymmetric flow field-flow fractionation with multi-angle light scattering system (AF4-MALS).

Measure the number density of adiposomes using an Eclipse 3 system containing an in-line vacuum degasser, HPLC isocratic pump, manual injection valve, UV detector at a wavelength of 280 nm, and MALS detector with 18 scattering angles from 14.4° to 163.3º at 658 nm.
Use PBS as the flow phase for AF4-MALS analysis.
Set the AF4-MALS conditions according to Table 12.
Dilute the adiposome suspension by a factor of 20-50 using PBS buffer.
Inject 30–50 μL of the diluted adiposome suspension into the AF4-MALS system.
Use the particle number density template to determine the number density of artificial LDs.
Determine the average diameter of artificial LDs by DLS technique.
Calculate the total surface area of droplets per mL assuming a spherical shape for artificial LDs.
Use the same procedure to determine the number density of natural LDs for normalization with artificial LDs.
Measure the average diameter of natural LDs/adiposomes using DLS technique.
Determine the total neutral lipid mass of natural LDs/adiposomes per mL using triacylglycerol assay kit or cholesterol assay kit, or both.
Calculate the total volume of droplets per mL using the total mass and average density of neutral lipids.
Estimate the number density of droplets by dividing the total volume of droplets by the volume of a single droplet.
Match the number density of specific protein on the surface of natural LDs and artificial LDs using gel electrophoresis.
Isolate natural LDs expressing the specific LD protein to be studied.
Mix 40 μL of isolated LD sample with 700 μL acetone and 300 μL chloroform.
Vortex the mixture vigorously.
Centrifuge the mixture at 20,000×g for 10 min.
Remove the liquid phase carefully after centrifugation.
Expose the protein precipitates to air until dry.
Mix the dried proteins with sample loading buffer for gel electrophoresis.
Determine the amount of purified recombinant protein using Coomassie Brilliant Blue staining.
Load the extracted sample on the same gel together with a dilution series of bovine serum albumin (BSA).
Analyze the protein bands using ImageJ.
Quantify the amount of recombinant protein using BSA as a reference.
Use Western blotting to normalize the specific protein on natural LD.
Apply Coomassie Brilliant Blue staining for both BSA and target recombinant proteins.
Replace Coomassie Brilliant Blue staining with Western blot if a commercial target protein is used as a reference.
Confirm the purity of recombinant proteins using alternative methods such as BCA protein assay kit.
Determine the concentration of recombinant proteins using the BCA protein assay kit when applicable.
Omit Day 2 procedure for artificial LDs if qualitative experiments are conducted only.
Avoid high protein concentrations to prevent artificial LD clustering.
Mix adiposome samples in each tube by gentle vortex.
Normalize the concentration of adiposomes to OD600 = 20.
Distribute equal 30 μL aliquots in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Thaw frozen proteins on ice.
Determine the protein concentration using BCA protein assay kit.
Add a range of volumes of the protein solution to tubes containing 30 μL adiposomes.
Add Tris-NaCl buffer to each tube to bring final volumes to 60 μL.
Vortex gently to mix aliquots three times.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000×g for 10 seconds.
Incubate all specimens at 4°C for 12 hours in the dark.
Isolate artificial LDs by centrifugation at 20,000×g, 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove infranatant using a gel-loading pipette tip carefully.
Resuspend isolated artificial LDs in 30 μL of Buffer B.
Repeat step to remove nonspecifically associated proteins twice.
Resuspend isolated artificial LDs in 800 μL of Tris-NaCl buffer per tube.
Vortex for 15 seconds.
Dilute Triton X-100 into 800 μL of Tris-NaCl buffer to a final concentration of 1% (v/v).
Prepare a dilution series by diluting protein stock solution with Tris-NaCl buffer containing Triton X-100.
Distribute the protein dilution series in a 96-well plate, with 200 μL per well and three replicates.
Centrifuge the plate at 3,000×g for 1 minute prior to measurement.
Prepare two-fold serial dilutions of adiposomes by diluting original adiposomes (OD600 = 20) with Buffer B.
Distribute the artificial LD suspension into a 96-well plate, with 200 μL per well and three replicates.
Determine the absorbance at 600 nm of artificial LD aliquots and adiposome aliquots using an EnSpire multimode plate reader.

Determine the fluorescence intensity of all specimens using the same plate reader with proper excitation and emission wavelengths for the protein under study, such as PLIN2-GFP (excitation 488 nm, emission 530 nm).
Construct a binding curve of proteins to adiposomes.
Correct the background absorbance of buffer from standards by scanning the blank buffer.
Create a calibration curve using RFU against the concentration of protein standards and generate a linear regression No.1.
Create a calibration curve using RFU against the absorbance at 600 nm of diluted serial suspension of adiposomes and generate a linear regression No.2.
Correct the background of adiposomes from samples using linear regression No.2.
Calculate the concentration of proteins bound to adiposomes using linear regression No.1.
Correct the concentrations of bound proteins by multiplying the dilution factor (roughly 13.3 in this study).
Measure OD600 of adiposomes after centrifuging/washing procedure.
Correct the number of droplets using the ratio of measured OD600 to theoretical OD600.
Dilute adiposomes with OD600 = 20 for 13.3 times and measure the corrected OD600 value.
Generate a saturation curve of bound protein concentration versus total protein concentration.
Use GraphPad Prism 7.0 software to render the Scatchard plot.
Calculate the concentration of free protein by subtracting the bound concentration from the total concentration.
Perform linear regression of Bound/Free versus Bound to yield slope = -KD-1, where KD is the equilibrium dissociation constant.
Determine the abscissa intercept as Bmax, the maximum saturation concentration of ligand binding sites.
